To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) charge neutral alpha matter is a quantum liquid with an EOS very similar to that of nuclear matter and that (ii) the alpha‐alpha interaction that is consistent with the scattering data and the α‐α resonance properties, i.e. the 7.65 MeV level, is not suitable for alpha matter calculations.
the alpha matter EOS is not consistent with the experimental saturation properties of nuclear matter and that a variational approach to the alpha matter EOS does not work.

the α‐α potentials with a repulsive core, which are the only ones that can produce saturation, are not compatible with the experimental scattering and resonance data and that the variational HNC calculations with gaussian correlations do not produce saturation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether the ground state of alpha matter at T=0 can be described as a quantum liquid of α‐particles.
a variational study of the ground state of charge neutral alpha clusters at T=0.

the search for a realistic α‐α interaction that is consistent with all available low energy α‐α data, and that can be used to calculate the EOS of alpha matter in the framework of a microscopic variational approach.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the variational method is not suitable to describe the EOS of alpha matter.
the variational approach is not able to provide a consistent description of the α‐alpha system and, hence, of the EOS of α matter.
the α‐α interaction does not exist and that α‐α matter is not a liquid.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the alpha matter at T = 0 cannot be described as a quantum liquid of alpha clusters.
the α‐α potentials proposed in the past and in the literature are not consistent with a variational description of α matter.
the alpha matter EOS is not consistent with the experimental constraints.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the α‐α potential that is best suited for the description of alpha matter is a repulsive potential that does not describe the scattering data and has an unbound state.
the variational HNC method with gaussian correlation is not suitable for studying the EOS of alpha matter.
the α‐α potential should be determined by fitting to the experimental data on the α‐α scattering and resonances, and then used in the variational approach to determine the properties of alpha matter.
